newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Energy Grp year earnings strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Energy Grp year earnings strong.

text.p: Energy Group Plc, the UK electricity and U.S. coal interests group spun off from conglomerate Hanson in February, will produce pro-forma year earnings on June 12, which should show healthy growth, analysts said.

The group, Britain's biggest electricity distributor, said at its debut on the stock exchange on February 24, that operating profits were 138 million stg, up 38 percent, in the three months to December 31, while it was still part of Hanson.

Analysts were expecting proforma pretax profits for the year of 401.4 to 443 million stg, with a dividend payout for the last quarter of 5.5 pence per share, making a nominal total year figure of 22 pence.
The market is likely to watch for updates on the performance of its power stations and for any deals to increase its portfolio, especially in the U.S., analysts said.

The Energy Group owns Eastern Electricity, a regional electricity supplier, and is the country's fourth largest generator after buying 6,000 megaWatts of capacity from National Power and PowerGen which they were forced to sell by competition authorities.
The company has said it expects growth to come from development of its power and energy trading business in the UK, the U.S. and Australia.
Its Peabody U.S. coal business is expected to provide little excitement after quarterly results reported at The Energy Group's debut were flat.
The company could also make further comments on the new Labour government's proposed one-off tax on excess profits of privatised utilities, analysts said.

Earlier this month, the company was reported to have told Treasury officials that it felt the fairest formula for levying the tax would be on shareholder gains in the first year after privatisation, leaving Recs to pay only around 13 percent of the total.
Eastern Electricity was one of the 12 Recs privatised by the former Conservative government.
